procedure.step: The Ministry of Economy and Tourism registers the factory (requires location outside a free zone, a MoIAT industrial licence, and a MoIAT letter confirming 40% domestic value added; takes about 3 working days).
procedure.authority: the Ministry of Economy and Tourism

procedure.step: The Ministry of Foreign Trade issues the Certificate of Origin for India through its e-service: log in to the ministry e-services portal, choose the Certificate of Origin for India service, fill in the application form, upload the required documents, pay the fee online, submit the application, and receive approval or a return with comments to correct; processing takes about one working day.
Certificate fee: AED 50 (band: invoice value up to AED 100000).
The competent authority issues the certificate prior to, at, or within five working days of the date of exportation; it is valid for twelve months from the date of issue and covers only one import.
The Indian importer claims the CEPA rate when filing the bill of entry and must hold origin information under CAROTAR 2020, including which origin criterion is claimed.
The exporter keeps origin records, including the cost breakdown, for at least five years starting from the end of the calendar year of the certificate's issue.

caveats.note: The '+' in the product-specific rule is read as 'and' (both tests must pass); the agreement does not define '+', so this is Mansha's interpretation.
Operations and final manufacture are the exporter's own declaration.
Factory declared in a free zone: likely not eligible for the ministry's factory registration; confirm with the ministry.
India charges duty on the assessable (CIF) value at import, so actual amounts will differ from the estimate shown.
CEPA rates reduce Basic Customs Duty (BCD) only. IGST, GST compensation cess, SWS and any anti-dumping or safeguard duty still apply.
The CEPA rate applies only if the product qualifies under the rules of origin and a valid certificate of origin is presented.
The CEPA lowers the duty on this line but does not remove it.
'Direct labour cost' and 'direct overhead cost' are not defined in the agreement.
The agreement does not say whether the build-down and build-up methods use the same threshold, apart from the 5-point Ex-Works adjustment.

No official page read names the Ministry of Foreign Trade as the issuer of the India CEPA certificate specifically: its service page covers preferential certificates in general, and the India-specific page is still on moet.gov.ae.
That electronic certificates are accepted and uploaded to India's e-Sanchit system comes from CBIC Instruction 28/2022, which Mansha has read only through secondary reports.
The 40% value-added letter is a registration condition only; it is NOT the CEPA product-specific rule test, which is set per tariff line.
